intervals.label: deployment and first season
intervals.note: Deployed in the 2014-2015 austral summer (LAMBDA); the 2016 paper calls 2016 "its second year of observation (and first science season)", so the commissioning end is set at 2016 (year precision).
intervals.quote: BICEP3, the successor to BICEP2, was deployed to the Dark Sector Laboratory at Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station in the 2014-2015 Austral summer season.

intervals.label: science observations
intervals.note: Open-ended: the official BICEP/Keck publication list (checked 2026-10-26) includes SPIE 2024-2026 papers on calibration of "the BICEP3 and BICEP Array CMB Polarimeters from 2017 to 2024" and on BICEP data "from 2016 through 2024"; no source states that BICEP3 stopped observing.
intervals.quote: has been observing at the foreground-minimum 95 GHz since 2016

placements.note: Same mount as BICEP2: "BICEP3 occupies a separate mount previously used for BICEP2 on a nearby building" (arXiv:2110.00483).
placements.quote: BICEP3, the successor to BICEP2, was deployed to the Dark Sector Laboratory at Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station in the 2014-2015 Austral summer season.

diameter.quote: BICEP3 is a 520 mm aperture, compact two-lens refractor

sensor_count.quote: a full complement of 20 tiles of detectors (2560 TESs)

summary.plain: A 52-centimetre refracting telescope in the Dark Sector Laboratory at the South Pole with 2560 superconducting detectors at 95 GHz, the most sensitive BICEP/Keck instrument at that frequency.
summary.technical: Compact two-lens refractor, 520 mm aperture, 20 tiles (2560 TES bolometers) at 95 GHz, on the former BICEP1/BICEP2 mount in the Dark Sector Laboratory; science observations since 2016.

technology.quote: BICEP3 is a 520 mm aperture, compact two-lens refractor designed to observe the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at 95 GHz.
technology.value: Compact two-lens refracting telescope, 520 mm aperture, 95 GHz, with modular antenna-coupled TES focal-plane tiles.
